paragraphs: Goldman Sachs is a leading global financial institution that delivers a broad range of financial services to a large and diversified client base that includes corporations, financial institutions, governments and individuals. Our purpose is to advance sustainable economic growth and financial opportunity. Our goal, reflected in our One Goldman Sachs initiative, is to deliver the full range of our services and expertise to support our clients in a more accessible, comprehensive and efficient manner, across businesses and product areas.

When we use the terms "Goldman Sachs," "we," "us," "our" and "the firm," we mean The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc. (Group Inc. or parent company), a Delaware corporation, and its consolidated subsidiaries. When we use the term "our subsidiaries," we mean the consolidated subsidiaries of Group Inc. References to "this Form 10-K" are to our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025. All references to 2025, 2024 and 2023 refer to our years ended, or the dates, as the context requires, December 31, 2025, December 31, 2024 and December 31, 2023, respectively.

Group Inc. is a bank holding company (BHC) and a financial holding company (FHC) regulated by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (FRB). Our U.S. depository institution subsidiary, Goldman Sachs Bank USA (GS Bank USA), is a New York State-chartered bank.

We manage and report our activities in three business segments: Global Banking & Markets, Asset & Wealth Management and Platform Solutions. Global Banking & Markets generates revenues from investment banking fees, including advisory, and equity and debt underwriting fees, Fixed Income, Currency and Commodities (FICC) intermediation and financing activities and Equities intermediation and financing activities, as well as relationship lending and acquisition financing (and related hedges), investing activities related to our Global Banking & Markets activities and transaction banking. Asset & Wealth Management generates revenues from management and other fees, incentive fees, private banking and lending and investments. Substantially all of the revenues in Platform Solutions are from activities related to issuing credit cards to and raising deposits from Apple Card customers and related to businesses that have been exited.
The chart below presents our three business segments.

Beginning with the fourth quarter of 2025, we made certain changes to our segments as we continued to narrow our strategic focus with respect to consumer-related activities within Platform Solutions. The primary changes within our segments are as follows:
•Global Banking & Markets additionally includes the results from our transaction banking business, which are reported in Other (previously reported in Platform Solutions).

•Within Global Banking & Markets, results related to facilitating institutional primary loans for syndication and providing structured letters of credit to corporate clients are reported in FICC financing (previously reported in Other).

•Results from our Urban Investment Group, which makes investments in connection with our activities to satisfy requirements under the Community Reinvestment Act (CRA), are allocated across all three segments to reflect the shared nature of such requirements (previously reported in Asset & Wealth Management).

•Within Asset & Wealth Management, results from Equity Investments and Debt Investments are reported in aggregate, as we continue our transition from direct investments on our balance sheet to a scaled third-party funds-driven business.

Global Banking & Markets serves public and private sector clients and we seek to develop and maintain long-term relationships with a diverse global group of institutional clients, including corporations, governments, states and municipalities. Our goal is to deliver to our institutional clients all of our resources in a seamless fashion, with our advisory and underwriting activities serving as the main initial point of contact. We make markets and facilitate client transactions in fixed income, currency, commodity and equity products and offer market expertise on a global basis. In addition, we make markets in, and clear client transactions on, major stock, options and futures exchanges worldwide. Our clients include companies that raise capital and funding to grow and strengthen their businesses, and engage in mergers and acquisitions, divestitures, corporate defense, restructurings and spin-offs, as well as companies that are professional market participants, who buy and sell financial products and manage risk, and investment entities whose ultimate clients include individual investors investing for their retirement, buying insurance or saving surplus cash.

As a market maker, we provide prices to clients globally across thousands of products in all major asset classes and markets. At times, we take the other side of transactions ourselves if a buyer or seller is not readily available, and at other times we connect our clients to other parties who want to transact. Our willingness to make markets, commit capital and take risk in a broad range of products is crucial to our client relationships. Market makers provide liquidity and play a critical role in price discovery, which contributes to the overall efficiency of the capital markets. In connection with our market-making activities, we maintain (i) market-making positions, typically for a short period of time, in response to, or in anticipation of, client demand, and (ii) positions to actively manage our risk exposures that arise from these market-making activities (collectively, inventory).

We execute a high volume of transactions for our clients in large, highly liquid markets (such as markets for U.S. Treasury securities, stocks and certain agency mortgage pass-through securities). We also execute transactions for our clients in less liquid markets (such as mid-cap corporate bonds, emerging market currencies and certain non-agency mortgage-backed securities) for spreads and fees that are generally somewhat larger than those charged in more liquid markets. Additionally, we structure and execute transactions involving customized or tailor-made products that address our clients' risk exposures, investment objectives or other complex needs, as well as derivative transactions related to client advisory and underwriting activities.

headings: Market Developments and General Business Environment
Our businesses have been and may in the future be adversely affected by conditions in the global financial markets and broader economic conditions.
Our market-making activities have been and may in the future be affected by changes in the levels of market volatility.
Inflation has had and could in the future have a negative effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Our liquidity, profitability and businesses may be adversely affected by an inability to access the debt capital markets or to sell assets.

Our businesses have been and may in the future be adversely affected by disruptions or lack of liquidity in the credit markets, including reduced access to credit and higher costs of obtaining credit.
Reductions in our credit ratings or an increase in our credit spreads may adversely affect our liquidity and cost of funding.

Group Inc. is a holding company and its liquidity depends on payments and loans from its subsidiaries, many of which are subject to legal, regulatory and other restrictions on providing funds or assets to Group Inc.
Our businesses, profitability and liquidity may be adversely affected by deterioration in the credit quality of or defaults by third parties.
Concentration of risk increases the potential for significant losses in our market-making, underwriting, investing and financing activities.
Derivative transactions and delayed documentation or settlements expose us to credit risk, unexpected risks and potential losses.

A failure or disruption in our infrastructure, or in the operational systems or infrastructure of third parties, could impair our liquidity, disrupt our businesses, damage our reputation and cause losses.
The development and use of AI present risks and challenges that may adversely impact our business.
paragraphs: We face a variety of risks that are substantial and inherent in our businesses.
The following is a summary of some of the more important factors that could affect our businesses:
•Our businesses have been and may in the future be adversely affected by conditions in the global financial markets and broader economic conditions.

•Our businesses have been and may in the future be adversely affected by declining asset values, particularly where we have net "long" positions, receive fees based on the value of assets managed, or receive or post collateral.
•Our market-making activities have been and may in the future be affected by changes in the levels of market volatility.

•Our investment banking, client intermediation, asset management and wealth management businesses have in the past been adversely affected and may in the future be adversely affected by market uncertainty or lack of confidence among investors and CEOs due to declines in economic activity and other unfavorable economic, geopolitical or market conditions.

paragraphs: We generated net earnings of $17.18 billion for 2025, compared with $14.28 billion for 2024. Diluted earnings per common share (EPS) was $51.32 for 2025, compared with $40.54 for 2024. ROE was 15.0% for 2025, compared with 12.7% for 2024. Book value per common share was $357.60 as of December 2025, 6.2% higher compared with December 2024.

Net revenues were $58.28 billion for 2025, 9% higher than 2024, reflecting higher net revenues in Global Banking & Markets, partially offset by significantly lower net revenues in Platform Solutions. The increase in net revenues in Global Banking & Markets primarily reflected significantly higher net revenues in Equities, significantly higher Investment banking fees and higher net revenues in Fixed Income, Currency and Commodities (FICC). The decrease in net revenues in Platform Solutions reflected a reduction in net revenues of $2.26 billion from markdowns on the outstanding credit card portfolio related to the transfer of the Apple Card loan portfolio to held for sale and contract termination obligations in connection with the agreement to transition the program to another issuer, which was more than offset by a related reserve reduction in provision for credit losses. Net revenues in Asset & Wealth Management were slightly higher, reflecting higher Management and other fees, higher net revenues in Private banking and lending and, to a lesser extent, higher Incentive fees, largely offset by significantly lower net revenues in Investments.

Provision for credit losses was a net benefit of $1.11 billion for 2025, compared with net provisions of $1.35 billion for 2024. The net benefit for 2025 reflected a net release related to the Apple Card loan portfolio (including a reserve reduction of $2.48 billion related to the transfer of the Apple Card loans to held for sale, partially offset by net charge-offs during the year). Provisions for 2024 reflected net provisions related to the credit card portfolio (primarily driven by net charge-offs).

Operating expenses were $37.54 billion for 2025, 11% higher than 2024, primarily reflecting higher compensation and benefits expenses (reflecting improved operating performance) and higher transaction based expenses. Our efficiency ratio (total operating expenses divided by total net revenues) was 64.4% for 2025, compared with 63.1% for 2024.

During 2025, we returned a total of $16.78 billion of capital to common shareholders, including $12.36 billion of common share repurchases and $4.42 billion of common stock dividends. As of December 2025, our CET1 capital ratio was 14.3% under the Standardized Capital Rules and 15.1% under the Advanced Capital Rules. See Note 20 to the consolidated financial statements for further information about our capital ratios.

業務持續性與資訊安全
paragraphs: Goldman Sachs 是一家領先的全球性金融機構，為大量且多元化的客戶羣提供廣泛的金融服務，包括企業、金融機構、政府與個人。我們的宗旨是促進可持續的經濟成長與金融機會。我們的目標，反映在 One Goldman Sachs 初步計畫中，是以更易取得、更全面且更有效的方式，為客戶提供我們全部的服務與專業知識，橫跨各業務與產品領域。

當我們使用 "Goldman Sachs"、"we"、"us"、"our" 以及 "the firm" 這些詞語時，指的是 The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.（Group Inc. 或母公司），一家德拉瓦州公司，以及其合併後的子公司。當我們使用 "our subsidiaries" 這個詞語時，指的是 Group Inc. 的合併後子公司。提及 "this Form 10-K" 時，是指我們的年度報告表 10-K，為 2025 年 12 月 31 日結算年度。所有提及 2025 年、2024 年與 2023 年的參考，均指我們的結算年度，或根據上下文所需的日期，分別為 2025 年 12 月 31 日、2024 年 12 月 31 日與 2023 年 12 月 31 日。
Group Inc. 是一家受美國聯邦儲備委員會（FRB）監管的銀行控股公司（BHC）與金融控股公司（FHC）。我們的美國存款機構子公司 Goldman Sachs Bank USA（GS Bank USA）是一家紐約州特許銀行。

我們管理並報告我們的業務活動為三個業務分部：全球銀行與市場、資產與財富管理以及平台解決方案。全球銀行與市場的收入來自投資銀行費用，包括諮詢費用、股票與債務發行費用、固定收益、外匯與商品（FICC）中介與融資活動、股票中介與融資活動，以及關係貸款與收購融資（以及相關對沖）、與全球銀行與市場活動相關的投資活動與交易銀行業務。資產與財富管理的收入來自管理及其他費用、激勵費用、私人銀行與貸款以及投資。平台解決方案的幾乎所有收入均來自與向 Apple Card 客戶發行信用卡與從 Apple Card 客戶籌集存款相關的活動，以及已退出的業務。
下圖展示我們的三個業務分部。
自 2025 年第四季開始，我們對業務分部進行了一些變更，因我們持續縮小在平台解決方案內與消費者相關活動的戰略重點。我們業務分部的主要變更如下：
•全球銀行與市場進一步包含我們交易銀行業務的結果，該結果在其他（原先報導於平台解決方案）中報告。
•在全球銀行與市場內，與協助機構主要貸款 syndication 以及為企業客戶提供結構化信用證相關的結果，報告於 FICC 融資（原先報導於其他）中。
•來自我們的都市投資集團之結果，該集團進行投資以符合社區再投資法案（CRA）之要求，已分配至所有三個應報告分部，以反映此類要求之共通性（先前報導於資產與財富管理）。
•在資產與財富管理內，股權投資與債務投資之結果以總計方式報導，因我們持續從直接投資於資產負債表轉變為以第三方基金為主之規模化業務模式。

全球銀行與市場服務公部門與私部門客戶，我們致力於與多樣化的全球機構客戶建立並維持長期關係，包括企業、政府、州與地方政府。我們的目標是為機構客戶提供我們所有資源，以無縫方式進行，以我們的顧問與發行活動作為主要的初始接觸點。我們在固定收益、貨幣、商品與股票產品上進行市場製造，並在全球範圍內提供市場專業知識。此外，我們在主要股票、選擇權與期貨交易所進行市場製造，並處理客戶交易。我們的客戶包括企業，這些企業籌集資金以成長與強化其業務，並進行併購、資產處置、企業防禦、重整與分拆，以及專業市場參與者，這些參與者買賣金融產品並管理風險，以及投資機構，其最終客戶包括為退休而投資的個人投資者、購買保險或儲存閒置現金的個人。

作為市場製造商，我們為全球客戶提供數千種產品的價格，涵蓋所有主要資產類別與市場。有時我們會自己擔任買方或賣方，如果買方或賣方不易取得，有時我們會將客戶與希望進行交易的其他方連接起來。我們願意在廣泛的產品中進行市場製造、承擔資本並承擔風險，對我們的客戶關係至關重要。市場製造商提供流動性，並在價格發現中扮演關鍵角色，這有助於資本市場的整體效率。與我們的市場製造活動相關，我們維持（i）市場製造頭寸，通常為短暫期間，以回應或預期客戶需求，以及（ii）頭寸以主動管理因這些市場製造活動而產生的風險敞口（合稱為存貨）。

我們為客戶執行大量交易，這些交易在大型、高度流動的市場中進行（例如美國國庫券市場、股票市場及某些機構房貸過手證券市場）。我們也為客戶執行交易，這些交易在流動性較低的市場中進行（例如中型企業公司債、新興市場貨幣及某些非機構房貸過手證券市場），這些交易的利潤與費用通常較流動性較高的市場為高。此外，我們設計並執行涉及客製化或量身打造產品的交易，以解決客戶的風險敞口、投資目標或其他複雜需求，以及與客戶顧問與發行活動相關的衍生交易。

paragraphs: 本公司於2025年產生淨 earnings 為171.8億美元，較2024年的142.8億美元增加。稀釋後每股普通股 earnings (EPS) 為51.32美元，較2024年的40.54美元增加。ROE 為15.0%，較2024年的12.7%增加。每股普通股帳面價值為2025年12月的357.60美元，較2024年12月增加6.2%。

2025年淨營收為582.8億美元，較2024年增加9%，反映Global Banking & Markets 的淨營收增加，部分抵銷Platform Solutions 的顯著減少。Global Banking & Markets 的淨營收增加主要反映Equities 的顯著增加、Investment banking fees 的顯著增加以及Fixed Income, Currency and Commodities (FICC) 的淨營收增加。Platform Solutions 的淨營收減少反映因Apple Card loan portfolio 轉移至held for sale 以及合約終止義務，導致outstanding credit card portfolio 的markdowns 減少淨營收22.6億美元，此減少被相關credit loss provision 的備抵減少所抵銷。Asset & Wealth Management 的淨營收略微增加，反映Management and other fees 的增加、Private banking and lending 的淨營收增加，以及Incentive fees 的增加（程度較輕），主要抵銷Investments 的顯著減少。
備抵信用減損為 2025 年帶來淨利得 1.11 十億美元，與 2024 年的淨減損 1.35 十億美元相比。2025 年的淨利得反映與 Apple Card 貸款組合相關的淨釋除（包括因將 Apple Card 貸款轉移至持有待售而減少備抵信用減損 2.48 十億美元，部分抵銷年度內的淨壞帳損失）。2024 年的減損反映與信用卡組合相關的淨減損（主要因淨壞帳損失驅動)。
2025年營運費用為375.4億美元，較2024年增加11%，主要反映compensation and benefits expenses 的增加（反映營運表現改善）以及transaction based expenses 的增加。我們的效率比率（總營運費用除以總淨營收）為2025年的64.4%，較2024年的63.1%增加。
2025年，本公司共回饋167.8億美元資本給普通股股東，包括123.6億美元普通股買回以及44.2億美元普通股股息。截至2025年12月，本公司CET1資本比率根據Standardized Capital Rules 為14.3%，根據Advanced Capital Rules 為15.1%。有關資本比率的進一步資訊，請參閱財務報表附註第20項。

headings: 市場動態與整體營運環境
本公司之業務已並可能於未來因全球金融市場及更廣泛經濟條件而受到不利影響。
本公司之市場造市活動已並可能於未來因市場波動程度之變化而受到影響。
通貨膨脹已並可能於未來對本公司業務、營運結果及財務狀況產生負面影響。
本公司之流動性、獲利能力及業務可能因無法取得債務資本市場資金或出售資產而受到不利影響。
本公司之業務已並可能於未來因信貸市場之中斷或流動性不足而受到不利影響，包括信貸取得之減少及信貸取得成本之提高。
本公司信用評級之降低或信用 spreads 之增加可能對本公司之流動性及資金成本產生不利影響。
Group Inc. 為一間控股公司，其流動性取決於子公司所支付之款項及貸款，許多子公司受法律、法規及其他限制，無法提供資金或資產予 Group Inc.
我們的業務、獲利能力及流動性可能因第三方信用品質惡化或違約而受到不利影響。
風險集中會增加我們在市場做市、承銷、投資及融資活動中產生重大損失的潛在可能性。
衍生交易及文件延遲或結算，會使我們面臨信用風險、未預見風險及潛在損失。
我們的基礎建設或第三方運營系統及基礎建設若發生故障或中斷，可能影響我們的流動性，幹擾我們的業務，損害我們的聲譽，並造成損失。
人工智能的發展與應用帶來風險與挑戰，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 我們面臨許多風險，這些風險對我們的業務而言是重大且內在的。
以下為一些可能影響我們業務的重要因素摘要：
• 我們的業務已並可能未來受到全球金融市場及更廣泛經濟條件的不利影響。
• 我們的業務已並可能未來受到資產價值下降的影響，特別是在我們持有淨『長』部位、收取基於管理資產價值的費用，或提供或張貼擔保品的情況下。
• 我們的市場做市活動已並可能未來受到市場波動程度變化的影響。
• 我們的投資銀行、客戶中介、資產管理及財富管理業務過去已並可能未來受到市場不確定性或投資者及企業首席執行官信心不足的影響，這是因為經濟活動下降及其他不利的經濟、地緣政治或市場條件所致。
